README.md.overview: Top-level project description. It names the Frontiers in Earth Science manuscript on intermediate-depth seismicity beneath the Himalayas, points to the Zenodo QuakeML catalog, and routes readers to the Python and GMT instructions.

sections.title: Project description
sections.explanation: Explains that the repository holds Python and GMT scripts that reproduce the manuscript figures. The study applies advanced detection techniques to continuous waveforms to characterize intermediate-depth seismicity beneath the central Himalayas. The catalog itself lives on Zenodo in QuakeML format.

sections.title: Run instructions and caveat
sections.explanation: Links to the Python and GMT READMEs, which split the project in two halves. The note warns that the scripts reproduce this publication only and must be modified for other uses.

python/README.md.overview: Setup guide for the Python half. It builds a conda environment and then runs the two driver scripts, Figures_5-9.py and Figure_10.py.

sections.title: Conda environment
sections.explanation: Recommends conda and creates a `him_seis` environment pinned to Python 3.7 and eqcorrscan 0.4.2, plus obspy, matplotlib, numpy, pandas, pyproj, shapely and basemap. The old Python and eqcorrscan pins matter because the scripts import eqcorrscan utilities.

sections.title: Running the figures
sections.explanation: Two commands produce the figures: `python Figures_5-9.py` for figures 5 to 9 and `python Figure_10.py` for figure 10.

sections.title: GMT notes
sections.explanation: The tail of the file mentions the files directory and the separate gmt5 conda environment for the GMT scripts, and shows how to run Figure_1.sh. This duplicates the GMT README.

python/Figures_5-9.py.overview: Main driver script for figures 5 to 9. It reads the QuakeML catalog, defines polygon sub-regions, and delegates the actual plotting to temporal_plots and migration_plots. It does little computation itself and mainly orchestrates.

sections.title: Imports and figure style
sections.explanation: Imports obspy, the two local plotting modules and numpy, then sets global matplotlib font and default figure size (13 by 8) that apply to every later plot.

sections.title: Catalog loading
sections.explanation: Builds the catalog path from the current working directory, so the script must be run from the folder containing `quakeml/`. `read_events` parses the QuakeML file into an obspy Catalog.

sections.title: Sub-region polygons
sections.explanation: Defines `coords` as consecutive pairs of lists (latitudes, then longitudes) for four clusters plus a whole-area box. Later calls slice this list in twos, e.g. `coords[0:2]`, to select one polygon.

sections.title: Figures 5 and 6
sections.explanation: Figure 5 (magnitude versus time with cumulative counts) and Figure 6 (inter-event times) are single calls that take the full catalog and the polygons.

sections.title: Figure 7 frequency-magnitude
sections.explanation: Cuts sub-catalogs using polygons, merges the first two clusters into `catalog_one`, and sorts it by origin time. Then `multi_mfd_plot` compares cluster 1, cluster 3 and the full catalog.

sections.title: Figures 8 and 9 migration
sections.explanation: Defines cross-section endpoints as lon/lat arrays and calls `plot_migration` for two catalogs: cat_2 with profile CD (swath 200 km) and cat_1 with profile AB (swath 250 km). Events are sorted by time first. Some defined profiles (AA, BB) are unused.

sections.title: Figure 10 pointer
sections.explanation: Notes that figure 10 is produced by the separate Figure_10.py script.

python/temporal_plots.py.overview: Library of catalog helpers and temporal/statistical plots used by Figures_5-9.py. It extracts event attributes, filters events by polygon, and produces inter-event time, magnitude-versus-time and magnitude-frequency (b-value) figures using eqcorrscan utilities.

sections.title: Imports
sections.explanation: Pulls in matplotlib, numpy and two eqcorrscan functions, `calc_b_value` and `calc_max_curv`, for magnitude-of-completeness work.

sections.title: Catalog helpers
sections.explanation: `get_cat_details` flattens an obspy Catalog into lists of time, lat, lon, depth (converted from m to km) and magnitude, using the last origin and magnitude of each event. `cut_cat` builds a shapely Polygon from (lat, lon) lists and keeps events whose epicentre lies inside it. `create_lines` makes vertical stem lines for plots.

sections.title: Inter-event times plot
sections.explanation: `interevent_times_single_cluster` computes time gaps between consecutive events in each polygon region and plots them for Figure 6.

sections.title: Magnitude versus time
sections.explanation: `mag_vs_time_plus_cumulative` draws magnitude stem plots against time with cumulative event counts for each polygon sub-catalog, producing Figure 5.

sections.title: b-value fit
sections.explanation: `calc_bvalues` selects magnitudes at or above Mc + 0.4 and up to the maximum, then fits a line to log10 of the cumulative counts with `np.polyfit`. The slope gives the b-value.

sections.title: Multi-catalog MFD plot
sections.explanation: `multi_mfd_plot` computes Mc via maximum curvature and the maximum magnitude for three catalogs, then overlays histograms and fitted cumulative distributions for Figure 7.

python/migration_plots.py.overview: Implements the seismicity migration analysis behind Figures 8 and 9. It projects events onto strike and dip profile lines and plots distance versus time. Distance maths is done directly in the script.

sections.title: Setup and style
sections.explanation: Imports and sets a larger default figure size (15 by 10) and a subplot rectangle dict.

sections.title: Distance helper
sections.explanation: `dist_calc` gives the 3D distance in km between two (lat, lon, depth) points. It uses a flat-Earth approximation with a mean-latitude cosine correction, as the docstring admits, and credits Calum Chamberlain.

sections.title: Profile projection
sections.explanation: Inside `plot_migration`, the nested `calculate_profile` projects each event onto the line between two reference points. It scales longitude by cos(lat), rejects events farther than the swath width (degrees = km / 111) or beyond the line ends, and returns along-line distance, depth, magnitude and time.

sections.title: Event selection
sections.explanation: Keeps only events between 40 and 110 km depth, collects their attributes and parses origin times. Then it calls `calculate_profile` once for the strike line and once for the dip line.

sections.title: Three-panel figure
sections.explanation: Dot sizes scale with magnitude (x70). The top panel plots along-strike versus perpendicular distance coloured by along-strike distance. The two lower panels plot dip and strike distances against time. It then saves a PNG named by profile and shows it.

python/Figure_10.py.overview: Standalone driver for Figure 10, a 3D view of earthquake hypocentres and stations. It adapts eqcorrscan-style 3D plotting functions to show two catalogs (this study and Diehl et al. 2017) together with the station inventory.

sections.title: Imports and style
sections.explanation: Imports obspy readers and sets the same global matplotlib font and figure size as other scripts.

sections.title: Polygon split
sections.explanation: `cut_cat` is a variant that returns both the events inside the polygon and the remainder, so the rest can be plotted in another colour.

sections.title: Figure finaliser
sections.explanation: `_finalise_figure` is a copy of an eqcorrscan helper: it sizes the figure, optionally titles, saves and shows it, then closes it. Note that it refers to a `Logger` not defined in this file, which would fail if `save=True` were used.

sections.title: Single-catalog 3D plot
sections.explanation: `obspy_3d_plot` and `threeD_seismplot` extract station and event coordinates and draw them in a matplotlib 3D axes.

sections.title: Two-catalog 3D plot
sections.explanation: `obspy_3d_plot_2cats` and `threeD_seismplot_2cats` extend the above to plot catalog 1, the remainder of catalog 1 outside the region, and catalog 2 with different markers.

sections.title: Script body
sections.explanation: Reads the main catalog, the Diehl et al. 2017 catalog and station XML files, splits by polygon, and calls the two-catalog 3D plot.

python/supporting_material/plot_1D_veloc.overview: Standalone script that plots four 1D velocity models (Nepal, Tibet, a gradient model and IASP) used for earthquake location. It is hard-coded data and plotting rather than catalog analysis.

sections.title: Imports and style
sections.explanation: Imports obspy, numpy and matplotlib and sets the standard figure style.

sections.title: Layer definitions
sections.explanation: Lists of Vp, Vs and layer-top depths per model, plus the step-line versions (`l_*`) where each value is repeated so that the plot shows velocity jumps as vertical steps.

sections.title: Vp/Vs ratios
sections.explanation: Computes Vp/Vs per model with loops. The IASP loop divides by `l_Vs_grad` rather than `l_Vs_iasp`, which looks like a copy-paste bug, though the ratio is not used in the final plot.

sections.title: Plot and save
sections.explanation: Plots Vp and Vs versus depth with different line styles, inverts the depth axis and saves a PNG to a hard-coded desktop path. Commented code outlines an unused Vp/Vs panel.

python/supporting_material/plot_catalog_.overview: Standalone script that summarises catalog quality: a hypocentral depth histogram and a multi-panel details figure. It helps judge the reliability of the catalog used in the main figures.

sections.title: Setup
sections.explanation: Imports, working directory and figure style.

sections.title: Depth histogram
sections.explanation: `plot_depth_histos` converts origin depths to km, draws a 2 km-bin histogram, and marks the mean and 90th percentile with vertical lines.

sections.title: Catalog details figure
sections.explanation: `plot_cat_details` collects per-event statistics such as the number of P picks and plots them in multiple panels.

sections.title: Run
sections.explanation: Loads the QuakeML catalog and calls both plotting functions.

gmt/README.md.overview: Short setup note for the GMT scripts. It creates the gmt5 conda environment and runs Figure_1.sh.

sections.title: Environment and first map
sections.explanation: Notes that a files directory holds the map input data, creates the environment from gmt5.yml, activates it and runs `bash Figure_1.sh`.

gmt/gmt5.yml.overview: Exported conda environment pinning GMT and its native dependencies so the shell scripts run reproducibly. It is a full dependency export, not a hand-written minimal file.

sections.title: Channels
sections.explanation: Uses conda-forge first and then defaults.

sections.title: Pinned dependencies
sections.explanation: A long list of exact package versions, including GMT, GDAL, GEOS and Ghostscript, along with their transitive libraries. Exact pins are the reason the environment recreates the original output.

sections.title: Prefix
sections.explanation: A machine-specific absolute prefix left over from the export. It is ignored when creating an environment elsewhere.

gmt/Figure_3AB.sh.overview: GMT shell script that draws Figure 3AB of the manuscript: two stacked depth cross-sections of Himalayan seismicity (A-A' and B-B'). It projects both the NonLinLoc (NLL) and double-difference (HDD) locations onto each profile line and overlays them with error bars. Note it reads files/NLL_locations.dat and files/HDD_locations.dat, which are not in the detailed list.

sections.title: Header and output name
sections.explanation: Banner comments describe the script (cross-sections of seismicity, by Konstantinos Michailos) and set the output EPS file name used by every later redirect.

sections.title: GMT defaults and base canvas
sections.explanation: Sets GMT map formats and fonts, then creates an empty 18x20 cm portrait basemap with -K so later layers can be appended to the same PostScript file.

sections.title: Profile A projection
sections.explanation: Defines start/end coordinates and a swath half-width of 50 km, then uses awk to extract the first five columns of the NLL and HDD location files and runs gmt project (-Fpz: distance along profile and depth) into temporary projection files. The -Q flag gives distances in km.

sections.title: Profile B projection
sections.explanation: Same procedure for the second, roughly perpendicular profile with a swath half-width of 60 km, producing projection2*.dat.

sections.title: Upper cross-section panel
sections.explanation: Plots HDD events as circles scaled by magnitude (-i0,1,2s0.025) on a depth axis flipped by -JX15/-5, adds dashed light-gray vertical error bars (column 4 scaled by 1.455), then draws the NLL events in black with red error bars on top. The -Y/-X offsets position the panel.

sections.title: Upper panel labels
sections.explanation: Adds the profile endpoint labels and the swath-width annotation with pstext heredocs.

sections.title: Lower cross-section panel
sections.explanation: Repeats the plotting recipe for the second profile, shifting down with -Y-7 and using its own distance range and width.

sections.title: Lower panel labels
sections.explanation: Endpoint labels and swath annotation for the second profile.

sections.title: Finalize and clean up
sections.explanation: Closes the PostScript with an empty -T layer, converts it to PDF via psconvert, opens it with evince, and deletes the EPS and temporary projection files.

gmt/Figure_3CD.sh.overview: GMT shell script that draws Figure 3CD of the manuscript: two stacked depth cross-sections of Himalayan seismicity (C-C' and D-D'). It projects both the NonLinLoc (NLL) and double-difference (HDD) locations onto each profile line and overlays them with error bars. It is structurally identical to Figure_3AB.sh, differing only in profile coordinates, labels and panel widths (the lower panel uses -JX11.31/-5).

sections.title: Header and output name
sections.explanation: Banner comments describe the script (cross-sections of seismicity, by Konstantinos Michailos) and set the output EPS file name used by every later redirect.

sections.title: GMT defaults and base canvas
sections.explanation: Sets GMT map formats and fonts, then creates an empty 18x20 cm portrait basemap with -K so later layers can be appended to the same PostScript file.

sections.title: Profile A projection
sections.explanation: Defines start/end coordinates and a swath half-width of 50 km, then uses awk to extract the first five columns of the NLL and HDD location files and runs gmt project (-Fpz: distance along profile and depth) into temporary projection files. The -Q flag gives distances in km.

sections.title: Profile B projection
sections.explanation: Same procedure for the second profile (D-D') with a 50 km half-width, producing projection2*.dat.

sections.title: Upper cross-section panel
sections.explanation: Plots HDD events as circles scaled by magnitude (-i0,1,2s0.025) on a depth axis flipped by -JX15/-5, adds dashed light-gray vertical error bars (column 4 scaled by 1.455), then draws the NLL events in black with red error bars on top. The -Y/-X offsets position the panel.

sections.title: Upper panel labels
sections.explanation: Adds the profile endpoint labels and the swath-width annotation with pstext heredocs.

sections.title: Lower cross-section panel
sections.explanation: Repeats the plotting recipe for the second profile, shifting down with -Y-7 and using its own distance range and width.

sections.title: Lower panel labels
sections.explanation: Endpoint labels and swath annotation for the second profile.

sections.title: Finalize and clean up
sections.explanation: Closes the PostScript with an empty -T layer, converts it to PDF via psconvert, opens it with evince, and deletes the EPS and temporary projection files.

gmt/files/all_stations.txt.overview: Merged station list for all seismic networks used in the study, one station per line with network, code, latitude, longitude, elevation, site name and operating period. It supplies the station triangles for the GMT maps and is the union of the per-network sta_*.txt files.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column description and the IRIS DMC data center comment. Lines starting with # are comments.

sections.title: Station records
sections.explanation: Whitespace-separated records such as 'IC LSA 29.7031 91.127 3660.0 Tibet, China ...'. Start/end times use ISO format; open-ended stations end at 2599-12-31. Site names contain spaces and commas, so only the first columns are safe to parse for plotting.

gmt/files/sta_HiCLIMB.txt.overview: Station list for the HiCLIMB (network XF) temporary network, in the same format as all_stations.txt (network, station, lat, lon, elevation, site, start, end). It is used to plot this network's stations on the study maps.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column names.

sections.title: Station records
sections.explanation: One line per HiCLIMB (network XF) station with coordinates and deployment window, which documents when each station was recording.

gmt/files/sta_HIMNT.txt.overview: Station list for the HIMNT (network YL, 2001-2002) temporary network, in the same format as all_stations.txt (network, station, lat, lon, elevation, site, start, end). It is used to plot this network's stations on the study maps.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column names.

sections.title: Station records
sections.explanation: One line per HIMNT (network YL, 2001-2002) station with coordinates and deployment window, which documents when each station was recording.

gmt/files/sta_NAMASTE.txt.overview: Station list for the NAMASTE (network XQ, Kathmandu region, 2015-2016) temporary network, in the same format as all_stations.txt (network, station, lat, lon, elevation, site, start, end). It is used to plot this network's stations on the study maps.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column names and data-center comment.

sections.title: Station records
sections.explanation: One line per NAMASTE (network XQ, Kathmandu region, 2015-2016) station with coordinates and deployment window, which documents when each station was recording.

gmt/files/catalogs/GANSSER_cat.txt.overview: Earthquake catalog from the GANSSER network in Bhutan (2013-2014). Each row is a located event with hypocenter, location uncertainties, origin time, local magnitude and quality metrics.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column names: event ID, lat, lon, depth (km), uncertainties in meters, date/time parts, Mlv magnitude, type, RMS, azimuthal gap, nearest-station distance and number of observations.

sections.title: Event records
sections.explanation: Fixed-column event rows such as '201301001 27.545232 88.558239 41.859 ...'. Note that some depths are negative and some uncertainties are very large, so quality filtering (RMS, GAP, Nob) may be needed before plotting.

gmt/files/catalogs/HIMNT_cat.txt.overview: Earthquake catalog from the HIMNT experiment, with a compact format of origin time, latitude, longitude and depth only. It supplies epicenters for the seismicity maps.

sections.title: Header
sections.explanation: Column names: year, month, day, hour, minute, seconds, latitude, longitude, depth.

sections.title: Event records
sections.explanation: One event per line, e.g. '2001 10 01 06 26 49.201218 28.813375 87.410329 25.25'. There are no magnitudes or uncertainties in this file.

gmt/files/catalogs/ISC_catalog.txt.overview: Reviewed ISC Bulletin event search results for the Himalayan region, in comma-separated form. It gives regional background seismicity with multiple magnitude estimates per event from different agencies.

sections.title: Search header
sections.explanation: Comment lines recording ISC citation guidance, search type (rectangular, reviewed bulletin) and the column header for event ID, author, date, time, lat, lon, depth, depth-fixed flag, and repeated author/type/magnitude triples.

sections.title: Event records
sections.explanation: Each row starts with the ISC event ID, prime-hypocenter author, date, time, position and depth, followed by a variable number of magnitude entries (mb, mbtmp, ML, ...), so rows have differing numbers of fields.

gmt/files/catalogs/focal_mechanisms/READ.overview: Short index of the focal mechanism data files stored beside it, listing each file with its literature source and time span. It explains where the beach-ball data for the maps comes from.

sections.title: File inventory
sections.explanation: Lists Chandra historical data (1505-1886), Baranowski, Chen and Kao, Harvard CMT, Holt 1995 (instrumental and historical), Kumar (1997 event), Molnar 1989 and 1990, and the NEI/CNSS catalog, each with its citation and years covered.

gmt/files/him/README.txt.overview: Documentation for HimaTibetMap-1.0, the active fault database (Taylor, Yin, Styron, Okoronkwo) from which the thrusts, normal, dextral and sinistral fault GMT files derive. It explains plotting, compilation method and data sources.

sections.title: Title and credits
sections.explanation: Names the database and its authors.

sections.title: Plotting the data
sections.explanation: Explains the KML, GMT and ESRI Shapefile versions: GMT files are plotted with psxy -M, and kinematics with -Sf. The shapefile uses a styles file from UC Davis.

sections.title: Database compilation
sections.explanation: Describes how structures were drawn in ArcMap over remote sensing imagery (ASTER, Landsat, SPOT, CORONA, SRTM) and from the literature. Precision is several kilometers, so it suits regional rather than local plots.

sections.title: Sources by structure type
sections.explanation: Tabulates faults by class (thrusts, fold-thrust belts, extensional systems, right- and left-slip faults, sutures, volcanics) with their references, and notes that unnamed faults come from Taylor et al. or remote sensing.

sections.title: Works cited
sections.explanation: Bibliography for the references above. Some accented characters appear garbled due to encoding.

gmt/files/him/thrusts.gmt.overview: GMT multi-segment vector file with thrust fault traces for the Himalaya-Tibet region, derived from HimaTibetMap-1.0. It is plotted as lines on the maps, with other fault classes held in sibling files.

sections.title: OGR/GMT header
sections.explanation: Header comments identify the GMT vector format, bounding box, WGS84 projection and the attribute schema (Id, Name, Type, ltype, X, Y, Source) from the GDAL conversion.

sections.title: Fault segments
sections.explanation: About 206 features, each starting with a '>' separator line followed by longitude/latitude vertices, for instance beginning near 82.31 E, 36.59 N. Plot with psxy -M.

gmt/files/him/normal_faults.gmt.overview: A GMT multisegment vector file (OGR_GMT format, GLINESTRING) holding normal fault traces for the Himalayan region, in WGS84 lon/lat. It is one of the HimaTibetMap fault datasets used by the GMT map scripts to overlay faults, as described in the tour's Faults and Color Palette step. The file is large (1480 lines), so only the header and first segments are explained here.

sections.title: OGR_GMT header
sections.explanation: Comment lines beginning with `# @` carry OGR metadata. `@VGMT1.0 @GLINESTRING` declares the GMT version and line geometry. `@R` gives the bounding region (lon 68.67 to 113.41, lat 25.39 to 41.30). `@Jp` and `@Jw` store the projection as a PROJ string and WKT (WGS84 longlat). `@N` and `@T` list the attribute names (Id, Name, Type, ltype, X, Y, Source) and their types. `# FEATURE_DATA` marks the start of the geometry.

sections.title: First fault segment
sections.explanation: A lone `>` starts each segment. The following `# @D` line holds the pipe-separated attributes for that feature, here Id 0 of type `normal` with ltype 1211 and a representative X/Y point. The lines after it are `lon lat` coordinate pairs tracing the fault, which GMT plots as a polyline.

sections.title: Repeating segments and tail
sections.explanation: The rest of the file repeats the same pattern: a `>` separator, an `# @D` attribute line, then the vertices. There are many segments. The tail shows coordinates near lon 89.4 to 89.6, lat 28 to 28.3 (Bhutan area). Because every segment follows this format, GMT commands such as `psxy` can draw the whole file in one call.

gmt/him.cpt.overview: A GMT color palette table (CPT) that maps elevation in metres to RGB colors for hypsometric shading of the Himalaya topography. It is borrowed from the France Wikimedia topographic map and translated to CPT form by J.J. Green, under CC BY-SA 3.0. It goes with the fault data in the tour's Faults and Color Palette step.

sections.title: Provenance and license
sections.explanation: The header comments credit the original author (Eric Gaba) and the translator, give the CC BY-SA 3.0 license, and note the source SVG. The `# COLOR_MODEL = RGB` line tells GMT to read the color columns as RGB values. The file name inside is `france.cpt`, so the palette was not made for the Himalaya.

sections.title: Elevation color bands
sections.explanation: Each row is `z_low r g b z_high r g b`. Both ends of a band have the same color, so the bands are flat steps and not a gradient. The palette starts with greens at 0 to 500 m. It moves through yellows and tans to browns and ends in near-white above 7000 m, up to 8000 m. Band widths vary, from 500 m at low elevation to 1000 m or 500 m higher up.

sections.title: Background, foreground, NaN
sections.explanation: `B` is the background color (black) for values below the range. `F` is the foreground (white) for values above 8000 m. `N` is the color for NaN or missing data (red), which makes holes in the grid easy to see.

gmt/Figure_1.sh.overview: A GMT (Generic Mapping Tools) shell script that draws Figure 1, the map of the seismic networks used in the study of intermediate-depth earthquakes beneath the Himalaya (Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, southern Tibet). It layers topography, faults, catalog seismicity, published focal mechanisms, station symbols, a legend and a regional inset into a single EPS, then converts it to PDF. Each GMT call appends to the same file using -K/-O, so the order of the commands is the stacking order of the map layers.

sections.title: Header, GMT settings, region
sections.explanation: Sets the output name and global GMT parameters (degree format, Helvetica fonts, plain frame). It defines the study region, 83-90E and 26-30N, and a 6-inch Mercator projection in shell variables so later calls can reuse them. The duplicated `gmt set` lines are harmless repetition.

sections.title: Basemap, topography and faults
sections.explanation: `pscoast` with no `-O` creates the output file and the basemap, which is the only call that uses `>`; every later call uses `>>`. `grdimage` drapes the 3-arc-second Tibet DEM using the `him.cpt` palette. A second `pscoast` adds borders and a scale bar, and three `psxy` calls draw thrusts, normal faults and dextral faults with front-style (-Sf) symbols.

sections.title: Catalog seismicity, colorbars, countries
sections.explanation: `makecpt` builds a viridis `seis.cpt` for depth from 40 to 110 km. `awk` filters two catalogs to events deeper than 50 km: HIMNT as red circles and the NEMRC candidates as black crosses. The symbol size column is rescaled with `-i...+s0.03`. Two `psscale` bars show topography and hypocentral depth, and a here-document labels the countries.

sections.title: Historical focal mechanisms
sections.explanation: Each published event follows the same pattern. A `psxy` leader line joins the true epicenter to a displaced label position. A depth-colored square marks the epicenter, `psmeca -Sa` draws the beachball at the displaced position (the columns are lon, lat, depth, strike, dip, rake, magnitude), and `pstext` adds a Roman-numeral ID. The events covered here are the 1988 Udayapur, 1986, 1991 and 1992 events plus the 1973 and 1976 mechanisms. The commented lines keep the earlier magnitude-and-year labels. Colors come from `seis.cpt` through `-Z`.

sections.title: GCMT and Alvizuri mechanisms
sections.explanation: Adds the 2005 and 2010 GCMT events, then three larger GCMT events (1980, 2003, 2011) plotted in one `psmeca` call without leader lines, and finally the Alvizuri 2002 M3.7 event. The comments record each source and its catalog ID. Labels are numerals that presumably correspond to a table in the paper.

sections.title: Diehl moment tensors
sections.explanation: `psmeca -Sm` plots full moment-tensor solutions from Diehl et al. as a block of rows. Each row gives position, depth, six tensor components, an exponent, and the position again. Several mechanisms from Bhutan and further east are in this block.

sections.title: de la Torre 2007 mechanisms
sections.explanation: Seven small events from de la Torre et al. (2007) repeat the leader line, epicenter square, beachball and label recipe. Labels are XIII to XVIII with some IDs skipped. Beachballs are offset from the epicenters, so labels do not overlap in the dense cluster near 87-88.5E.

sections.title: Seismic stations
sections.explanation: For each network `awk` extracts lon and lat (columns 4 and 3) from a station file and `psxy` draws them: Hi-CLIMB used as semi-transparent blue triangles, not-used Hi-CLIMB as outlined triangles, and HIMNT, the Bhutan pilot experiment and IC as inverted triangles in red or orange shades. The `-t` flag controls transparency.

sections.title: Legend, labels, scales, Everest
sections.explanation: `pslegend` reads a here-document that defines the network legend (with operating periods) and the candidate-event symbols. Further `pstext` calls label the MFT and DCFZ structures. A vector arrow with the text `45 mm/yr` shows plate convergence, azimuth 22.1 degrees. A column of circles builds a magnitude scale, and an X marks Mount Everest as a reference.

sections.title: Regional inset and finalization
sections.explanation: Re-defines the region and projection variables for a 2.75-inch inset of 70-100E and 25-40N, shifted with `-X0 -Y10.25`. It repeats the coast, topography and fault layers with different colors, labels INDIA and ASIA, and draws a rectangle for the study area. `psxy -T -O` closes the PostScript without `-K`, `psconvert` makes a cropped PDF, `evince` opens it, and `rm` deletes the intermediate EPS and CPT.

gmt/Figure_2.sh.overview: A GMT script that draws Figure 2, a seismicity map of the same Himalayan study region (83-90E, 26-30N) separating high- and low-quality deep events from shallow ones, with a zoomed inset of the main cluster showing cross-section traces A-D. The header comment says 'European Alps', which appears to be a copy-paste leftover; the code plots Himalayan data. It follows the same -K/-O layering scheme as Figure_1.sh and reuses many of its focal mechanism blocks.

sections.title: Header, settings, gray topo palette
sections.explanation: Same output and font setup as Figure 1 but with the west edge at 83.05. It also builds `topo.cpt`, an inverted gray palette over 0-9000 m. `topo.cpt` is created here, but the grids are drawn with `him.cpt`, so it is only cleaned up at the end. The header text mentions the European Alps, which does not match the data.

sections.title: Basemap, topography, faults, cluster box
sections.explanation: Creates the basemap, drapes the Tibet DEM with `him.cpt`, adds borders and a scale bar, and labels the countries. A thin rectangle (86.3-88.4E, 27.6-28.85N) marks the main cluster that the later inset zooms to. The three fault datasets are drawn with the same styles as in Figure 1.

sections.title: Station symbols
sections.explanation: Plots HIMNT, Hi-CLIMB, the Bhutan pilot network and IC stations in semi-transparent white so they stay visible but unobtrusive over the topography. A commented-out block shows the unused Hi-CLIMB not-used set.

sections.title: Seismicity layers and scales
sections.explanation: Builds a viridis depth palette with 5 km steps. Shallow high-quality events (under 40 km) are drawn as `+` marks. Deep low-quality events are plotted as black-outlined circles, and `All_events.dat` as depth-colored circles scaled by magnitude through `-i0,1,2,3s0.07`. After that come the MFT and DCFZ labels, a depth colorbar, an Everest marker and a 45 mm/yr convergence arrow.

sections.title: Historical focal mechanisms
sections.explanation: Reuses the Figure 1 recipe of leader line, epicenter square, `psmeca` beachball and numeral label for the 1988 Udayapur, 1986, 1991, 1992, 1973 and 1976 events. Coordinates and mechanisms are identical to Figure 1, so the two figures can be compared directly.

sections.title: GCMT and Alvizuri events
sections.explanation: Draws the 2005 and 2010 GCMT events, the 1980, 2003 and 2011 GCMT events in a batch, and the Alvizuri 2002 M3.7 event. The commented-out lines record the original magnitudes and years, and the labels use Roman numerals.

sections.title: de la Torre and Diehl mechanisms
sections.explanation: An empty `psmeca` block holds commented-out de la Torre data (the ones actually plotted follow). The seven de la Torre events then repeat the leader-line recipe, and a final `psmeca -Sm` block plots only the first seven Diehl moment tensors, a subset of what Figure 1 shows.

sections.title: Legend and magnitude scale
sections.explanation: `pslegend` explains the circle and plus symbols (high-quality and low-quality deep events, high-quality shallow events). Note that the legend text does not reflect the viridis depth coloring. A column of scaled circles with M=5 and M=1 labels forms the magnitude key.

sections.title: Zoom inset and traces A and B
sections.explanation: Redefines the region as 86.3-88.4E, 27.6-28.85N and starts a new 3.5-inch map shifted up with `-Y11`. It re-plots topography, coast, deep events and all events, and shallow events. Shell variables hold the start and end points of the A-A' and B-B' cross-section traces, which are drawn as dashed lines with labels via `pstext -TO`. The `width` variables are assigned but not used here.

sections.title: Traces C and D and finalization
sections.explanation: Adds the C-C' and D-D' trace lines in the same way, then marks Everest. `psxy -T -O` closes the PostScript, `psconvert -Tf -A` creates a cropped PDF, `evince` opens it, and `rm` deletes the EPS, `seis.cpt` and `topo.cpt`.

gmt/files/sta_HiCLIMB_not_used.txt.overview: HiCLIMB (XF) stations that were not used in the analysis, retained for reference.

gmt/files/sta_HiKNet.txt.overview: Station list for the HiKNet (ZO) network in western Nepal, 2014-2016.

gmt/files/sta_IC.txt.overview: Station list for the IC network; header comments only, no station entries.

gmt/files/sta_IN.txt.overview: Station list for the IN network; header comments only, no station entries.

gmt/files/sta_NCS.txt.overview: Single-entry station file for NK network station KKN at Kakani, Nepal.

gmt/files/sta_NQ.txt.overview: Station list for the NQ network in Nepal, including Kanti Path in Kathmandu.

gmt/files/sta_bhutan_pilot.txt.overview: Station list for the 2002-2003 Bhutan pilot (XA PASSCAL) deployment.
